subject: Privacy boundary and capacity mapping — MedSecure hosting options
messages:
From: Rajeev Kapoor <rajeev.kapoor@medsecure.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: security@medsecure.com
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial discovery — hosting posture question

Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Our security team asked for a concrete comparison between Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity) and Redwood Private (VPC/on‑prem) specifically for the upcoming pilot that will process PHI. Primary asks from our side:

- Expected GPU footprint and node counts for a 10k DAU pilot and for a 100k DAU production ramp
- Operational separation surface (networking, audit logs, KMS ownership)
- Typical lead times and procurement triggers for Dedicated vs Private
- Any SLA differences and options for fallback to hosted in an incident

Can you share a short mapping and an estimate? Procurement may want an early cost band to budget. I attached the security baseline they shared (see MedSecure_Security_Baseline.pdf).

— Rajeev

Attachments: MedSecure_Security_Baseline.pdf (PDF, 320KB)

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial discovery — hosting posture question

Rajeev —

Really helpful checklist, thanks. High level answer up front: for a PHI‑sensitive pilot we usually recommend Private (VPC) for data residency and customer‑managed KMS; Dedicated is a good compromise when teams want predictable throughput with simpler procurement but need strict tenant isolation.

I pulled a short mapping and a strawman capacity estimate for both paths and attached a sizing workbook and a diagram (hosted_vs_private_capacity_sheet.xlsx, sizing_diagram.png). Those are conservative — we designed the numbers to allow a 30% burst buffer and KV cache hit assumptions at 40%.

Two asks from you so we can firm numbers:
1) Expected average tokens per request and 95th percentile token length for the pilot workload (or a sample trace)
2) Whether MedSecure will accept Redwood‑managed KMS for the pilot or requires customer KMS/HSM right away

If you want, we can schedule a 30m capacity walkthrough early next week.

Thanks,

Date: Fri, 23 Jun 2028 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Privacy boundary and capacity mapping — internal notes

Quick internal notes before the walkthrough:

Assumptions used in the workbook (call these out during the call):
- Pilot traffic shape: 10k DAU, 1% conversion to an inference request every 15 minutes => ~6.7 tokens/sec average per model per user at peak; estimate ~1.2M tokens/day
- Model choice: open LLM family (quantized 4-bit variant) — 32‑token average response, 100 tokens 95p
- KV cache hit: 40% (conversation reuse expected for triage flows)
- Safety/regression buffer: reserve 30% capacity for retention and burst

Private (VPC) implications:
- Customer manages KMS/HSM, private control plane — adds procurement + setup (2–6 weeks depending on network approvals)
- Larger baseline GPU footprint: dedicated p4d or H100 mixes depending on latency SLOs; more ends up being dedicated nodes scaled for isolation

Dedicated implications:
- Redwood runs control plane and KMS optionally; faster turnaround (1–3 weeks start) but some customers push for bring‑your‑own‑KMS for PHI
- Lower ops overhead for customer; can provide SLA credits on request

I'll be on the call to walk through the workbook. Karthik — can you verify the assumed instance mix and expected throughput numbers on the sheet?

— Marissa

(No attachments)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Jun 2028 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Privacy boundary and capacity mapping — internal notes

Marissa / Hannah —

Verified the model mix in the sheet. Notes to call out when we present to Rajeev:

- For the pilot (10k DAU) a small Dedicated pool of 4x H100‑80GB equivalent (or 6x A100‑80GB) will cover steady state with 30% headroom given our token assumptions and batching. Estimate: sustained 1.2M tokens/day -> 3000 tokens/sec sustained with bursts to 8k TPS.
- For Private (VPC) with customer KMS: plan for 6x H100 nodes to keep the isolation boundary and maintain identical SLOs — additional nodes required because we cannot share prefetched KV caches across customers.
- Lead time: Dedicated reserved pool ready in ~7–10 business days after signed SOW and sizing signoff. Private VPC onboarding frequently takes 3–6 weeks due to network/VPN and KMS integration milestones.
- Fallback: route lower‑priority requests to hosted multi‑tenant model variants with reduced token caps in an incident; need explicit contract language for cross‑fallthrough and billing.

I left inline comments in the workbook on the chosen instance types and burst policies.

— Karthik

Attachments: hosted_vs_private_capacity_sheet.xlsx (updated commentary)

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 25 Jun 2028 16:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Privacy boundary and capacity mapping — MedSecure next steps

Rajeev / Emily —

Thanks for the baseline; we've reviewed with engineering and procurement and attached a short recommendation pack (hosted_vs_private_capacity_sheet.xlsx, sizing_diagram.png). High‑level recommendation:

1) Pilot (10k DAU): Proceed with Dedicated reserved pool (4x H100 equivalent) + customer KMS optional — this minimizes procurement friction and lets MedSecure validate traffic patterns while preserving tenant isolation at the compute plane. Expected onboarding: 7–10 business days after SOW.

2) Production ramp (100k DAU): Transition to Private VPC for full data residency and customer‑owned KMS/HSM. Estimate baseline of 24x H100 equivalent nodes (banded across AZs) to maintain 95p latency targets and allow for regional failover. Plan lead time: 3–6 weeks for network and KMS procurement.

3) Contract asks we recommend: explicit cross‑fallback clause (to hosted multi‑tenant model) for incident mitigation, defined KV cache warmup window, and SLAs for failover latency.

Next steps: proposal and SOW draft for the pilot (we can reuse the sizing workbook as an annex). Would you prefer Redwood to manage KMS for the pilot to speed start, or does MedSecure require customer KMS from day one?

If you approve, I'll loop legal and solutions engineering and send a pilot SOW draft by EOD Wednesday.

Cheers,
Hannah Schmitt
Sales, Redwood Inference
